title: Navigate the DeepSeek Ecosystem & Architecture
summary: Understand DeepSeek V3/R1 architecture, Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), DeepSeekMoE, and open-weight availability.
objectives: Explain Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and how it compresses KV cache footprint.
Understand DeepSeekMoE architecture with fine-grained expert routing and shared experts.
Compare DeepSeek V3 general capabilities with DeepSeek R1 deliberate reasoning behaviors.

sections.title: Architectural Innovations: MLA & DeepSeekMoE
paragraphs: DeepSeek V3 achieves high efficiency through Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), which compresses keys and values into low-dimensional latent vectors, drastically reducing GPU memory consumption during inference.
DeepSeekMoE activates only a subset of specialized experts per token while maintaining dedicated shared experts for common linguistic knowledge.

code.label: DeepSeek V3 Architecture Highlights
code.code:
Total Parameters: 671B
Activated Parameters per Token: 37B (256 routed experts + 1 shared expert)
KV Cache Compression: MLA Low-Rank Projection (93% memory reduction vs standard MHA)

questions.prompt: What primary efficiency does Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) provide during inference?
choices: It compresses key-value states into low-dimensional latent vectors, reducing KV cache VRAM by over 90%.
It converts text tokens directly into raw binary machine code.
It eliminates the need for internet connectivity entirely.
It forces models to output exactly 10 tokens per second.
questions.explanation: MLA projects keys and values into a compressed latent space during inference, dramatically cutting KV cache memory overhead.
